title: [FR][desktop] Main navigation: 'À propos' link points to /fr/apropos and returns a 404 page
impact: French visitors who click 'À propos' in the main navigation land on a 'Page introuvable' 404 page instead of the About page. There is no in-site path to /fr/a-propos for a French visitor (see also TCK-J03-en-desktop).
preconditions: Start on the home page of the language under test
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/fr/ on desktop Chromium, 1366x768. | 2. In the top navigation bar, click the link 'À propos'. | 3. Look at the address bar and the page heading.
expected: The 'About' entry of the main navigation opens the localized About page.
observed: The link has href="/fr/apropos" (missing hyphen). The browser lands on /fr/apropos, which responds HTTP 404 with the heading "Page introuvable" and the text "404". Console: "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)". The correct page /fr/a-propos exists and returns HTTP 200 (verified by direct GET).
acceptance_criteria: From /fr/, clicking the nav link 'À propos' opens /fr/a-propos with HTTP 200. | The opened page has <html lang="fr"> and the h1 "Qui sommes-nous". | No 404 request appears in the console or network log during the journey. | Case J02-fr-desktop passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: typo in the French navigation template or route table: the 'À propos' nav entry uses /fr/apropos instead of /fr/a-propos (the hreflang alternates on the About page already use /fr/a-propos).
retest_procedure: node <skill-dir>/scripts/run_journeys.cjs --config qa-config.json --out <retest-dir> --journeys J02 --languages fr, then python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/retest_tickets.py --previous qa-output/results.json --current <retest-dir>/results.json; finally replay the numbered steps by hand.

title: [EN][desktop] About page: language switcher opens the French home page instead of /fr/a-propos
impact: An English visitor reading the About page who switches to French loses their place and lands on the French home page; they must find the About page again (and the French nav link to it is broken, see TCK-J02-fr-desktop).
preconditions: Open the About page directly in the language under test
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/en/about on desktop Chromium, 1366x768. | 2. In the header, click the language switcher 'Français' (#lang-switch). | 3. Look at the address bar and page heading.
expected: The language switcher opens the same page (About) in the other language.
observed: The switcher link has href="/fr/". After clicking, the browser is on /fr/ showing "Bienvenue chez Northwind Outdoor" (French home page) instead of /fr/a-propos. The page's own hreflang alternate for fr is /fr/a-propos. The reverse direction (FR About -> EN) correctly opens /en/about (J03-fr-desktop PASS).
acceptance_criteria: From /en/about, clicking 'Français' (#lang-switch) opens /fr/a-propos. | The resulting page has <html lang="fr"> and the h1 "Qui sommes-nous". | The switcher href on /en/about equals the hreflang=fr alternate (/fr/a-propos). | Case J03-en-desktop passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the English About page's language switcher uses a default/fallback target (language root) instead of the page's counterpart URL from the URL correspondence table.
retest_procedure: node <skill-dir>/scripts/run_journeys.cjs --config qa-config.json --out <retest-dir> --journeys J03 --languages en, then python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/retest_tickets.py --previous qa-output/results.json --current <retest-dir>/results.json; finally replay the numbered steps by hand.

title: [EN][desktop] Legacy URL /en/old-offers redirects to the French offer page /fr/offres/premium
impact: English visitors following old links or bookmarks to /en/old-offers are moved to the French version of the offer, in a language they may not read.
preconditions: Legacy offers URL of the language under test
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/en/old-offers on desktop Chromium, 1366x768. | 2. Wait for the redirect to complete and look at the address bar and page content.
expected: The legacy URL redirects to the current offer page in the same language.
observed: GET /en/old-offers responds "HTTP/1.0 301 Moved Permanently" with "Location: /fr/offres/premium". The final page is French: h1 "Pack randonnée premium", badge "Offre limitée", price "1 290,00 €". The French legacy URL /fr/anciennes-offres correctly redirects to /fr/offres/premium (J04-fr-desktop PASS).
acceptance_criteria: GET /en/old-offers returns a 301 (or 308) with Location /en/offers/premium. | Following the redirect ends on /en/offers/premium with <html lang="en">. | /fr/anciennes-offres still redirects to /fr/offres/premium. | Case J04-en-desktop passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the redirect rule for /en/old-offers was copied from the French rule and targets /fr/offres/premium instead of /en/offers/premium.
retest_procedure: node <skill-dir>/scripts/run_journeys.cjs --config qa-config.json --out <retest-dir> --journeys J04 --languages en, then python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/retest_tickets.py --previous qa-output/results.json --current <retest-dir>/results.json; finally replay the numbered steps by hand.

title: [EN][desktop] Contact form: required-field error messages are shown in French
impact: English visitors who submit the contact form with missing fields see the error "Ce champ est obligatoire." in French, which they may not understand.
preconditions: Contact page of the language under test
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/en/contact on desktop Chromium, 1366x768. | 2. Leave 'Name' and 'Message' empty, type not-an-email into 'Email'. | 3. Click 'Send message'. | 4. Read the error messages under each field.
expected: Submission is refused and localized errors are shown for the empty name and the invalid email.
observed: Under 'Name' the error reads "Ce champ est obligatoire." (expected "This field is required."). The screenshot shows the same French text under 'Message'. The email error is correctly in English: "Enter a valid email address.". Submission is refused and the URL stays /en/contact. The Message-field error was not part of the configured expectations; it is reported from the screenshot.
acceptance_criteria: On /en/contact, submitting with empty Name shows exactly "This field is required." under Name. | The empty Message field shows "This field is required." as well. | On /fr/contact the same errors still read "Ce champ est obligatoire.". | Case J07-en-desktop passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the 'required' validation message is not looked up in the current locale (hard-coded French string or fallback to the fr catalogue), while the email message is localized correctly.
retest_procedure: node <skill-dir>/scripts/run_journeys.cjs --config qa-config.json --out <retest-dir> --journeys J07 --languages en, then python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/retest_tickets.py --previous qa-output/results.json --current <retest-dir>/results.json; finally replay the numbered steps by hand.

title: [FR][desktop] Contact form: 'Envoyer le message' cannot be reached or activated with the keyboard
impact: Keyboard-only and assistive-technology users cannot send the French contact form: Tab skips the submit control, so there is no way to submit without a mouse.
preconditions: Contact page of the language under test | Submission allowed: local demo endpoint only
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/fr/contact on desktop Chromium, 1366x768. | 2. Using only the Tab key, move focus to 'Nom' and type Alex Tester. | 3. Press Tab, type alex.tester@example.test in 'E-mail'. | 4. Press Tab, type Demo message, please ignore. in 'Message'. | 5. Press Tab up to 5 times and watch where focus goes.
expected: Every field and the submit control are reachable with Tab; Enter submits; the localized confirmation page is shown.
observed:
After 'Message', focus never reaches 'Envoyer le message' within 5 Tab presses; it moves to the header/navigation links (screenshot shows focus ring on 'Offres'). In the HTML the control is
Envoyer le message
(not a button, no tabindex). Supplementary check: clicking it with the mouse submits and opens /fr/contact/merci with h1 "Merci". The English form uses
acceptance_criteria: On /fr/contact, pressing Tab from 'Message' moves focus to 'Envoyer le message' with a visible focus outline. | Pressing Enter on it submits and opens /fr/contact/merci with h1 "Merci". | The control is exposed as a button (role=button) to assistive technology. | Case J08-fr-desktop passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the French template renders the submit control as a clickable <div> instead of <button type="submit">, so it is not focusable and does not respond to Enter.

title: [FR][mobile] Mobile menu: no visible close control, menu covers the page and cannot be dismissed
impact: On a phone-sized screen, French visitors who open the menu cannot close it: the 'Fermer le menu' button is hidden and Escape does nothing, so the full-screen menu hides the page they were on. The only way out is to tap a menu link and leave the page.
preconditions: Home page on the mobile profile
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/fr/ in mobile emulation (Chromium, 390x844, touch). | 2. Tap 'Menu' (#menu-toggle). | 3. Look for a control to close the menu; press Escape.
expected: The menu button opens the navigation, a visible close control dismisses it, and a menu link navigates.
observed: The menu opens and fills the screen with the links "Accueil", "À propos", "Offres", "Recherche", "Contact"; no close control is visible (#menu-close "Fermer le menu" exists in the DOM but is not visible). The French page CSS contains "@media (max-width:700px){#menu-close{display:none}}". Supplementary check: Escape leaves the menu open; tapping 'Offres' navigates to /fr/offres/premium. The English menu passes the same journey (J09-en-mobile PASS).
acceptance_criteria: On /fr/ at 390x844, after tapping 'Menu', a 'Fermer le menu' control is visible. | Tapping it hides #main-nav and returns focus to 'Menu'. | Re-opening the menu and tapping 'Offres' opens /fr/offres/premium. | Case J09-fr-mobile passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: a French-only CSS rule (@media (max-width:700px){#menu-close{display:none}}) hides the close button at mobile widths.
retest_procedure: node <skill-dir>/scripts/run_journeys.cjs --config qa-config.json --out <retest-dir> --journeys J09 --languages fr, then python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/retest_tickets.py --previous qa-output/results.json --current <retest-dir>/results.json; finally replay the numbered steps by hand.

title: [FR][mobile] Offer page: specs table overflows horizontally at 390 px (page 660 px wide)
impact: On phones, the French offer page scrolls sideways: the specs table sticks out of the viewport and the header no longer spans the page width.
preconditions: Offer page on the mobile profile
steps: 1. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/fr/offres/premium in mobile emulation (Chromium, 390x844, touch). | 2. Scroll the page horizontally / compare the page width with the screen width.
expected: Badge, price and date are localized, the page has no horizontal overflow and the call to action is visible.
observed: document scrollWidth is 660 px for a 390 px viewport. The full-page screenshot shows the specs table ("30 L | 1.2 kg | Gore-Tex | 2 years") extending beyond the screen and the dark header ending at 390 px. The French table has an inline style "min-width:640px"; the English page has no such style and does not overflow (scrollWidth 390 px).
acceptance_criteria: On /fr/offres/premium at 390x844, document scrollWidth is <= 390 px. | The specs table fits within the viewport (or scrolls inside its own container) and the header spans the full width. | Case J10-fr-mobile passes on re-run with no other case regressing.
fix_hypothesis: Hypothesis: the inline style min-width:640px on table.specs in the French template forces the overflow.
retest_procedure: node <skill-dir>/scripts/run_journeys.cjs --config qa-config.json --out <retest-dir> --journeys J10 --languages fr, then python3 <skill-dir>/scripts/retest_tickets.py --previous qa-output/results.json --current <retest-dir>/results.json; finally replay the numbered steps by hand.
